page.layout: One page of text in two columns of running text, the left column set in a narrow measure with the right column in one block; in the left margin are small notes (marginal catchwords and a side heading "Terra tem peramen-tum"), and in the left margin a Roman numeral "III." and "IV." stand beside the text. Running head at top, page number at top left, catchword at foot right.

main_text.p: dispefcunt, Afiam, Africam, Europam, Americam. Alii in tres partes melius videntur diftinguere. 1. Continet terram nostram, seu Europam, Asiam, & Africam comprehendit. 2. Continet terram occiduam, seu Indiam novam, quam Americam dicunt. 3. Dicitur Australis ea, cujus littora late pervagata à Lufitanis perhibentur.

III.3. Terra respectu aquarum & marium distinguitur in continuam & solutam seu liberam: Continua dicitur quæ continuatis partibus etiam in fundo marium cohæret: libera vero quæ soluta à reliquis terræ partibus mari incumbit, ut Insulæ quædam feruntur in mari sustentari & fluctuare.
IV.4. Terra distinguitur in planam & montosam: ubi Terræ & montes nonnulli perpetuo & evidenti igne ardent.

Terra tem peramen-tumTemperamentum terræ non est frigidissimum, quippe quæ non est caloris vivifici expers. Hunc enim arguit. 1. Ejus fertilitas, quæ omnis generis germina producit: calorem hunc Sol excitat, promit & auget. 2. Metallorum productio in visceribus terræ, quæ non fit sine calore

page.notes: Page is a text page from a 17th-century Latin geography work (Libri Secundi). Marginal notes at left: "III.", "IV.", and the side note "Terra temperamentum" (set in the margin as "Terra tem peramen-tum"). The long s has been rendered as s throughout. Words in the first column, "Afiam", "Africam", "Europam", "Americam", "Asiam" were printed with long s and are copied as printed letters. The word "Insulæ" and similar s-forms have been normalised to plain s per the rules. The bottom catchword "calore" is printed at right below the last line. Some ink in the margin is show-through and omitted.
